correctness.rationale: In anchored coordinates a chosen A vertex is zero and the Euclidean Gram determinant is 1/n. For fixed A range r, B fills the cube [max_A-1,min_A+1]^q; exact anchored A-span sublevel measure p r^(p-1) yields beta-integral volume 2^(n-1)p!q!/(n-1)!. Conditional B ranges are scaled independent-uniform ranges with Beta(q-1,2) law; independence from Beta(p-1,q+1) A span yields the Dirichlet(p-1,q-1,2) law. Its Beta(2,n-2) slack marginal gives the exact tail. Independent Gamma variables with shapes p-1,q-1,2 prove the joint Gaussian-Gamma limit, including centering and independence; binomial unimodality proves extremizers. All formulas are exact for specified integers; finite geometry, lattice and rejection-sampling checks are corroboration, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The polar Lipschitz body is the natural metric dual of a canonical complete-bipartite symmetric edge polytope. Within-part oscillations and their residual total allowed cross-part gap are intrinsic, interpretable geometric observables. The precise Dirichlet factorization identifies a bipartition-universal Beta(2,n-2) slack despite polar volume varying by the large binomial factor, and the independent Gaussian/Gamma scaling distinguishes macroscopic class fluctuations from microscopic unused slack. These laws are a motivated geometric distribution statement, not arbitrary parameter slicing; they provide an exact finite-dimensional benchmark for sampling graph-Lipschitz polytopes. This value does not depend on exclusive novelty of the subsidiary volume normalizer.
